business: Night Shift: open-source app that runs a team's coding-agent pipelines overnight on their own computers and logins
by_segment: Tech lead at a small digital agency
Senior developer who picks the tools for a small team
Owner or managing director of a small agency who holds the budget
Founder or CTO of an early-stage startup
why_not: I already threw away most of the PRs that background agents opened for us, and running them overnight just means I triage the junk in the morning. A pre-alpha tool from one developer won't change that, and I don't have time to draw flows and pair machines.

I have a spare Mac mini, so I'd try the free self-hosted version before paying $99 a month. And a pre-alpha built by one developer running agents unattended on our paid quotas overnight is exactly the setup I fear will loop and burn tokens.
We already get scheduled agents and PRs out of Claude Code and GitHub with the seats the company pays for. Drawing pipelines in a separate tool is one more thing I have to maintain.

I already have a cron job calling claude -p that opens PRs, and it works well enough. A pre-alpha tool from one developer is not something I move my team's pipeline onto, and the free self-hosted version covers me anyway if I get curious.

I'd maybe self-host the open source version to poke at it, but I won't pay $99 for Cloud. My problem with background agents was never scheduling. It was that the PRs were junk, and a nicer pipeline doesn't prove it fixes that.

I already run claude -p from cron for the boring stuff, and the free self-hosted version covers anything more. $99 a month for someone else to host a scheduler is a hard sell when my token bill already hurts.

If it's Apache-2.0 and runs on my own boxes, I'd self-host it and never pay for Cloud. I'd maybe try the free version, but Claude Code and GitHub Actions already cover most of the scheduled-agent stuff.
